title: Technology in Daily Life
description: Describe how a device or app helps or creates an everyday problem.
objectives: Describe how a device or app helps or creates an everyday problem.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to describe how a device or app helps or creates an everyday problem. The central language is relative clauses and present tense integration. It belongs to the practical context of opinions, technology & social life. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A2, connect the main message to a time, reason, contrast, or result. Listen for context before choosing the tense or functional phrase. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: relative clauses and present tense integration

blocks.english: I use an app that tracks my appointments.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the technology in daily life exchange.

blocks.english: My phone is the device that I use most.
blocks.explanation: This technology in daily life model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the technology in daily life exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “I use an app that tracks my appointments.” and “My phone is the device that I use most.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled. Compare the time and viewpoint in each model, and use a linker when two ideas need a clear relationship. Avoid adding advanced forms when the lesson pattern already communicates the message accurately.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: relative clauses and present tense integration.
